c: Soul Eater places a circular black aura around the player that pulls particles and slowly pulses inward, dealing damage to enemies inside it.
Soul Eater has a larger increase in
and an increase in Base Damage.

acts similarly to Hitbox Delay for Soul Eater. Damage will be dealt instantly to an enemy if they have never been in the circle before, after which they cannot be hit by it again until Soul Eater's Cooldown is over, even if they temporarily leave its area.

Enemies hit by Soul Eater will take more knockback and be more vulnerable to freeze. If the enemy is not immune to debuff, each hit applies +0.3 knockback to the enemy until the maximum knockback they can take and -0.1 to freeze resistance until it reaches 0.

The debuffs applied by Soul Eater are its most useful ability late game. Strong enemies that take multiple hits to kill will be easier to keep at bay thanks to increased knockback, and some boss enemies can become vulnerable to freezing when kept in the circle for long enough.
Combined with a weapon to constantly knock enemies away, such as
, Soul Eater can enable the player to sit entirely still.

has natural synergy with Soul Eater; it decreases the enemy's resistance to freezing, allowing the Clock Lancet to freeze bosses, and even very powerful frozen enemies can easily be killed by keeping Soul Eater's area of effect over them.
If the player intends to stay idle, Soul Eater works well when paired with the
, as enemies that die instantly to Soul Eater may drop experience just out of reach of the player.
Soul Eater's aura can kill most weak enemies instantly. Killing swarms of weak enemies can lead to windfalls of Little Hearts which can increase the damage output of Soul Eater.
Because Soul Eater does not count any overhealing, you have to occasionally take damage and heal back up in order to gain stacks. Due to this, it does not pair well with
(for instance), the player can take less risk in taking a lot of damage, just to heal up easily to empower Soul Eater.
